 Order

These are first bail applications filed by the applicants- Navalkishore and Neeraj under Section 483 of BNSS/439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to Crime No.
107/2024 registered at Police Station - Daboh, District- Bhind (M.P.) for the offence punishable NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13938 2 MCRC-18789-2025 under Sections 363,
366-A, 376-D of IPC and Section 5/6 of POCSO Act.
Applicants are in custody since 5/4/2025.
2. As per the story of the prosecution, the present applicants alongwith main accused Jagdish Shakya committed rape upon the prosecutrix, who was aged about 16 years and 11 months on 16/5/2024.

Learned counsel for the applicants referring to various statements of prosecutrix recorded at different stages of prosecution, submitted that the prosecutrix has been changing her statement at various stages.

Initially when she was recovered on 30th May, 20024 and she was sent for MLC, in her statement recorded before the doctor, she submitted that main accused Jagdish Shakya alone committed act of rape upon her, though, names of present applicants were also taken by her.

Thereafter, in her statement recoded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C., again she repeated the Neeraj vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 8 July, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21623307/
1 same version and the allegation of rape was not levelled against the present applicants.

Thereafter,
in her statement recorded under Section 164 of Cr.P.C., she roped the present applicants also and made allegation of rape against them also.
Thereafter, her statement before the Court was recoded on 19/5/2025, wherein, she has totally denied recognizing the present applicants.
On being shown the present applicants, she has specifically stated that these two persons are not the same persons against whom she made allegations.
Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that trial is likely to take time and in view of the changing statement of the prosecutrix.
There are very bleak chances of their being convicted for the offences alleged against them.
The present applicants needs to be enlarged on bail.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13938 3 MCRC-18789-2025 3.
On the other hand, learned counsel for State as well as complainant opposed the application and prayed for dismissal of the same.

4. Having taken into consideration all the facts and circumstances of the case, period of custody undergone and that early conclusion of the trial is a bleak possibility and prolonged pre-trial detention being an anathema to the concept of liberty and the material placed on record does not disclose possibility of applicants fleeing from justice, though this Court is inclined to extend benefit of bail to the applicants but with certain stringent conditions.
5.

Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on merits of the case, this application is allowed and it is directed that applicants be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rs. One Lac only) each with one solvent surety each of the like amount to the satisfaction of concerned Trial Court.
The applicants will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:13938 4 MCRC-18789-2025 trial;
6. The applicants will not leave India without previous permission of the trial Court/Investigating Officer, as the case may be.
